title: "Session 3 · R objects"
subtitle: "Types, coercion, subsetting, missing values, and factors"
---

## Learning goals

By the end of this session, you should be able to predict the type and length of
an R expression, diagnose unintended coercion, subset vectors safely, distinguish
common missing/special values, and explain what a factor stores.

## Materials

- [Slides](slides.qmd)
- [Guided lab](lab.qmd)
- Lab starter—choose one: `starter/objects-lab.Rmd` or `starter/objects-lab.qmd`

Copy your chosen starter to `work/session03/` before editing it.

## Two dialects, one set of ideas

We begin with base R because types and subsetting are properties of R itself.
When a tidyverse tool gives a useful alternative, it is shown in a comparison
box. Either style is acceptable unless an exercise explicitly asks for one.
